text:
Lane Hutson is the reason Montreal's games tilt. The Montreal Gazette asked where the Canadiens would be without him, and our numbers have an answer: worse by a lot. He plays more than 25 minutes a night at 22, Montreal takes 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, and that's 11 points better than when he sits.

He has 24 points in 26 games, eight on the power play, and almost none of it looks like luck. His on-ice shooting is close to neutral and his points rate sits right in the middle of our talent range. Last season Evolving-Hockey rated him the most valuable defenseman in the league, 4.9 wins above replacement, while noting some of that ran ahead of his chances.

The recent stretch is quieter: 8 points in ten games against roughly 10 expected, with his ice time climbing toward 29 minutes in a few of them. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows the habit to watch: he carries the puck in on 54% of his entries.
headline: Hutson is the engine Montreal runs on
